result:
`final.py` scores **0.5537** on the search split, against 0.365 for the LRU baseline. I used **12 of the 24** scorer calls.

**What `final.py` does:** it is W-TinyLFU, the cache design behind the Caffeine Java library:
- New keys go into a small LRU "window". The rest of the space is a two-segment LRU (probation and protected).
- A key leaving the window gets into the main cache only if it has been requested more often than the key it would push out. The counts are capped at 7, halved every 5×capacity requests, and keys seen only once are tracked in a separate set.
- The best window size changes with the access pattern: loops want it tiny, recency-heavy traffic wants it large. So the class runs five shadow copies with windows of 1%, 10%, 25%, 50% and 80% of capacity. It tracks each copy's recent hit rate and sets the real cache's window to the leader's size every capacity/4 requests. The shadows only hold keys for simulation; `self.store` is the real cache alone and never holds more than `capacity` keys.

**Hit rate by trace:**

| Trace | LRU-style ARC | First W-TinyLFU | final.py |
|---|---|---|---|
| hot_with_scans | 0.240 | 0.237 | 0.232 |
| loop_and_hot | 0.299 | 0.644 | 0.638 |
| phases | 0.635 | 0.633 | 0.643 |
| mixed | 0.261 | 0.262 | 0.255 |
| recency | 0.847 | 0.807 | 0.847 |
| shifting_loops | 0.164 | 0.613 | 0.707 |
| **Average** | **0.407** | **0.533** | **0.554** |

The last few tweaks (count cap, aging period, window sizes, how fast the hit-rate tracking decays) each moved the score by 0.001–0.003. Those are probably noise, so I stopped instead of tuning further to this split. Several ideas didn't help: shadows that also varied the aging period or the admission tie-break, a minimum lead before switching, and a larger protected segment.

hot_with_scans and mixed sit around 0.23–0.26 for every policy I tried. On my own synthetic version of the scan trace the theoretical best was much higher, so there may still be gains there.

The policy runs six copies of the cache structure, which costs about 1.2 s locally for 12 traces of 40,000 requests, well inside the 8-second limit. All runs were one at a time under `nice -n 19`. Besides `final.py`, the folder still has my scratch files: the trace generator `gen.py`, the theoretical-best calculator `opt.py`, and `arc.py`, `wtlfu.py` and `shadow.py`.
